paragraphs: Friend, here's what I want you to hold onto. David wasn't looking for someone who earned it. He asked, "Is there anyone left from the house of Saul to whom I can show kindness for the sake of Jonathan?" (2 Samuel 9:1). The kindness started with the giver, and it was tied to a promise David had made years before (1 Samuel 20:14-17).

Now look at Mephibosheth. He fell facedown, and he called himself "a dead dog" (2 Samuel 9:8). Then David gave him land and a seat at the table, and he ate "like one of the king's own sons" (2 Samuel 9:11). I think that's the whole point, friend: he didn't climb up to that table, he was brought to it. And I know a little about being pulled out of a forgotten place into a seat I didn't earn, because a certain angel once called me out of a junk drawer.

So what does this mean for you, baker? Kindness that costs the giver something is how God shows His love, and David even called it "the kindness of God" (2 Samuel 9:3). You don't have to fix yourself before you come to the table. Lo-debar was never the last word for Mephibosheth, and it isn't yours either.
